monitor.looks: a thin flat computer monitor, far smaller than a television, not a bulky CRT TV
monitor.built: taken out of its stand and case, its bare thin screen panel built into the project as its display, far smaller than a television; no monitor stand, no TV

motherboard.built: a bare board mounted inside the build's case, its memory and drives fitted in; never an intact desktop PC standing in the scene

laptop.looks: a thin opened laptop computer with flat screen hinged to keyboard base, far smaller than a bulky CRT TV
laptop.built: taken apart and built in, its bare thin screen panel used as the display and its board hidden inside the build; never an open laptop, laptop case, lid or keyboard in sight

laptop memory.looks: a tiny memory stick far smaller than laptop keys and body, not a large green board

microcontroller board.looks: a tiny credit-card-sized bare board, far smaller than half a laptop width

relay module.looks: a tiny module with small cube relay, far smaller than a laptop

sound sensor module.looks: a tiny sensor module, far smaller than a laptop

temperature and humidity sensor module.looks: a tiny sensor module, far smaller than a laptop

ultrasonic distance sensor module.looks: a tiny distance sensor module, far smaller than a laptop

home_automation_server.correction: An opened 15-inch laptop about 35 cm wide on a home desk for house lights and schedules, with one small laptop memory stick to true small scale beside it; not a desktop tower, not a TV, no large circuit board.
home_automation_server.built: A small wall-mounted wooden box about 35 cm wide in a home hallway, the laptop taken apart inside it: its bare screen panel framed in the front showing house light and schedule icons, its board and memory hidden inside; no open laptop, laptop case, lid or keyboard; not a desktop tower, not a TV.

home_server.correction: An opened laptop about 35 cm wide on a wooden desk wired to a router with antennas and to one bare 2.5-inch hard drive about 10 cm long by a single cable for backup; memory inside laptop not shown; drive plain with no ethernet ports, no second drive, no extra box, not a desktop tower.
home_server.built: A small closed wooden box about 35 cm wide on a shelf beside a router with antennas, the laptop taken apart inside it: board and memory hidden inside, one bare 2.5-inch hard drive fitted in the box; no open laptop, laptop case, lid or keyboard; no second drive, not a desktop tower.

kitchen_dashboard.correction: A 24-inch 16:9 computer monitor about 55 cm wide wall-mounted above kitchen counter as dashboard, with opened laptop on counter wired to tiny credit-card-sized microcontroller board plus four tiny modules nearby including relay with cube; not a TV.
kitchen_dashboard.built: A bare thin screen panel about 55 cm wide framed and wall-mounted above the kitchen counter as an icon dashboard, the laptop's board hidden in a slim box behind it wired to a credit-card-sized board and four tiny modules; no open laptop, laptop case, lid or keyboard; not a TV.

smart_mirror.correction: an 18 inch 5:4 computer monitor, about 46 cm across the diagonal, hidden behind a two-way mirror in a slim wooden frame about 45 x 40 cm, hung at eye level on a hall wall above a small bench; only a clock and weather icons glow through the glass; a small mirror, not a TV; no words or logos
smart_mirror.built: a bare thin screen panel hidden behind a two-way mirror in a slim wooden frame, the laptop's board hidden inside the frame, hung at eye level on a hall wall above a small bench; only a clock and weather icons glow through the glass; no open laptop, laptop case, lid or keyboard; not a TV; no words or logos

arcade_table.correction: A 24-inch flat monitor (~53x30cm widescreen) laid flat face-up inside the wooden coffee-table box under full-size glass top, joystick modules flush beside it, opened laptop wired below, living-room table use; no upright monitor on top, not a TV stand.
arcade_table.built: A wooden coffee table with a bare thin screen panel about 53 cm wide laid flat face-up under its full-size glass top, joystick modules flush beside it, the laptop's board hidden inside the table box; no open laptop, laptop case, lid or keyboard; no upright monitor, not a TV stand.

match: custom nas from a spare desktop board
custom_nas.correction: Single full-size ATX motherboard (~30.5x24.4cm) mounted in open cube case as NAS with one full-length desktop memory stick in DIMM slot, 2.5-inch SSD in drive bay with SATA leads, small PCIe adapter with two M.2 drives in PCIe slot, ATX PSU; not two boards, no SSD on board.

retro_console.correction: Opened laptop (~35cm wide) on wooden desk cabled to 24-inch thin flat widescreen monitor (~53x30cm) beside it both showing retro gaming, two wired gamepads in front in use; no cartridge console, no CRT TV, no cartridges or extra boards.
retro_console.built: A slim wooden box under the TV holding the laptop's board, cabled to a thin flat 24-inch screen showing retro games, two wired gamepads in front in use; no open laptop, laptop case, lid or keyboard; no cartridge console, no CRT TV.

weather_station.correction: Large microcontroller board (~7x5cm) with square USB-B and DC barrel jack on breadboard on indoor desk wired to 3-pin temperature-humidity module, coin-cell clock module and breadboard power module with barrel input and USB-A in use; no tiny Nano-size board.

homework_workstation.built: A quiet desk with a bare thin screen panel framed upright on the desk as the display, the laptop's board hidden in a slim box under the desk, a plain keyboard and mouse in front; no open laptop, laptop case or lid; not a TV.

views.close-up: a close-up at arm's length; the parts at their real sizes side by side
views.from above: seen straight down from above; every part at its true size against the table or desk

negatives: no lettering, logos, brand names, model numbers or labels on any part, case or screen
the sizes are for scale only: no dimension lines, measurements or size labels written in the picture
